summary.one_liner: pywin32 provides Python access to many Windows APIs, including COM support, as a set of Python extensions for Windows.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes pywin32 as the Python for Win32 extensions, giving Python code access to many Windows APIs, including COM support. It points to adodbapi and isapi subpackage docs, and to an online version of the PyWin32.chm help file, with the note that much of the documentation is old. Type hints and signatures are available separately via types-pywin32, and type stubs live in typeshed. Installation is via pip, with an optional post-install script (pywin32_postinstall -install) for global installs that registers COM objects and services. The README also covers running as a Windows service, troubleshooting upgrade DLL errors, and building from source with Visual Studio. Versioning is incremental build numbers, and the project notes that licenses vary by file.
use_cases: run a Python script as a Windows service
register COM servers and services after install
how_to_run: python -m pywin32_postinstall -install  (global installs only, not in virtual environments)
notable: Wraps many Windows APIs for Python, including COM support
Post-install script registers COM objects and services for global installs
Type stubs are maintained in typeshed and types-pywin32 is available
Includes adodbapi and isapi components with their own docs
Builds on GitHub Actions artifacts since build 307
caveats: Binary .exe installers are no longer supported; build 306 was the last with them
Documentation is described as old and partly outdated
Running as a Windows service requires Python in a location the service account can access
